Commands: targeted runs such as `cd bot && python3 -m unittest tests.test_flow.ReactionTests.test_an_approve_comment_queues_a_suggestion_for_build`, then the full suite `cd bot && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` (the same command `bot selftest` runs, on 3.12 and 3.13). The existing suggestion tests (`test_suggestions_when_idle_up_to_the_cap`, `test_suggestions_open_issues_up_to_the_cap`, `test_a_suggest_request_is_answered_by_the_survey`) must stay green unchanged.

## Done when

- [ ] Diagnosis from step 1 is recorded (open count, `last_run`, blocking gate).
- [ ] `approve` comment on an open `bot:suggestion` issue queues a build; `reject` closes it; both reply and react as specified.
- [ ] Bare votes on other threads are ignored; duplicate/edit replays act once; low-trust votes do nothing.
- [ ] Footer, prompt, and README describe comment votes; the `bot:build` label path still works.
- [ ] The four new tests plus the full `cd bot && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` pass.
- [ ] The issue carries the `human` label (people build it; see Open questions), and no file outside the table changed.

## Risks

- Bare-word misfire: someone writing "approve"/"reject" in ordinary discussion. Contained by scoping to open issues that carry `bot:suggestion` and skipping quoted/fenced lines via `command_lines`; suggestion threads carry almost no discussion. Rejected alternative: requiring `@bot` or `/harness` prefixes, which the issue overrules ("as comments").
- Vote races: `approve` then `reject` (or reverse) in two comments. First vote wins by acting first, enforced by `claim`; the loser gets a truthful reply (already queued / already closed), never a double build, since `queue_build` on a closed issue refuses.
- Spend profile: surveys still obey `max_open`, the 20-hour interval, provider hours, and lane room; this change only lets votes free the cap. Rejected alternative: lowering the interval or raising the cap, which spends more model budget without the maintainer asking for it.
- Delivery: `deliver.py` refuses any change touching `forbidden_paths` (which include `bot/`), so the night bot itself cannot build or ship this; a person must (see Open questions). No game, engine, AI, catalog, migration, or client behavior changes, so replay, determinism, hidden information, and the web are unaffected.

## Open questions

- Who does it: this needs the `human` label (assigned to both people by triage), because every file in the table is under `bot/`, which the night bot may not change — its deliver step refuses such a change. The issue's "Who does it" field was left as "Decide later", so please confirm by labelling `human`; the night bot must not take it.
- Nothing else: exact vote words (`approve`/`reject`, case-insensitive, whole line), trust level (maintainer, same as `build`), close reason (`not planned`), and unchanged cadence switches are all settled above; no maintainer decision blocks the work once `human` is set.
